methodologyNotes: Roster of 13 high-search camping tent models spanning ultralight backpacking and family car-camping (2P through 6P). Specs re-verified June 2026 against manufacturer product pages (Coleman, Cascade Designs/MSR, NEMO, Kelty, Marmot, ALPS, Big Agnes) and major retailers (REI, Walmart, Sherper's) plus review outlets (CleverHiker, SectionHiker, Treeline Review, Switchback Travel, Wilderness Times, Adventure Alan). packaged_weight_lb is packed/total weight in pounds (not minimum trail weight); floor_area_sqft is interior sleeping area; peak_height_in is interior standing height in inches; doors is integer count; rainfly_included boolean; seasons is the manufacturer rating string. Corrections this pass: North Face Wawona 6 price fixed 550->585 (current REI price; draft itself noted Scheels $585); REI Base Camp 4 peak height 60->63 in, floor 60->59 sqft, and packaged weight 16.88->17.35 lb to match REI's published 17 lb 5.6 oz spec. Eureka Copper Canyon LX 6 retained as a discontinued legacy model (Johnson Outdoors exited US/Canada Eureka consumer retail Oct 2024; residual-stock pricing ~$192-206, last published ~$198). REI Half Dome SL 2+ retained as a discontinued/verified model (replaced by Half Dome 2+); priceUsd null (no active MSRP). All accessedAt 2026-06-20.

products.name: Durston X-Mid 2 Tent
products.priceNote: Switchback Travel review (last updated Dec 23, 2025) lists "Price: $319" for the Durston X-Mid 2, and repeats "$319" in its comparison table. Durston's own product page was unreachable (HTTP 503 bot wall), so this dated-review figure is used.
products.provenance: Switchback Travel's review (last updated Dec 23, 2025) covers the current 2-person silpoly X-Mid 2 — confirmed as the exact model via "Durston X-Mid 2", "Capacities: 1P, 2P", the 15D silpoly fly, and the 92 x 52 in rectangular footprint, which distinguishes it from the Dyneema 'Pro' variant and the 1P version. It states verbatim: Price $319, packaged weight 1 lb 15 oz (= 1.94 lb), floor area 33.2 sq ft, peak height 48 in, with dual-door entry and a full-coverage rainfly. Durston's manufacturer page returned HTTP 503 (bot protection, also unreachable by the gate), and Adventure Alan's review describes an earlier generation (32 sq ft, 44 in peak, 2.4 lb, parallelogram footprint) so its conflicting figures were deliberately excluded; releaseDate is null because the 2018 debut has been superseded by 2025/2026 updates with no clean single release year stated.

products.name: NEMO Aurora Highrise 4P Tent
products.priceNote: US MSRP $399.95 for the 4-Person, stated verbatim on nemoequipment.com ("4-Person - $399.95"). GearJunkie's dated review corroborates the price point (Aurora Highrise is "$50 less" than the $450 North Face Wawona 4). Frontenac Outfitters (Canada) lists it at CAD $499.99.
products.provenance: NEMO's US product page (nemoequipment.com) confirmed model identity and price: the Aurora Highrise 4-Person is a standing-height family car-camping tent with two large doors/vestibules, listed at $399.95. Frontenac Outfitters' spec table for the exact 4P model verified floor area 62.5 sq ft, peak height 75 in, packed weight 15 lb 14 oz (15.88 lb), 2 doors, 3-season rating, and an included rainfly (68D PU polyester, 1200mm; 150D PU polyester floor). A dated GearJunkie review (June 25, 2025) independently corroborated 62.5 sq ft floor / 75 in height and the ~$400 price point ($50 under the $450 North Face Wawona 4). No explicit launch year was stated on any fetched page, so releaseDate/release are null.

products.name: Mountain Hardwear Mineral King 3 Tent
products.priceNote: CleverHiker's Sept 25, 2024 review of the Mountain Hardwear Mineral King 3 lists "Price: $400". Mountain Hardwear's own product pages (standard 2102591 and all-season 2063621) both returned a 404 "wrong turn" page, so no manufacturer MSRP was captured; REI listing 403'd.
products.provenance: Treeline Review's Oct 2, 2024 long-term review of the Mountain Hardwear Mineral King (3-person) confirmed the exact model and its specs verbatim: "Floor space: 42.5 square feet", "Peak height: 48 inches", "Weight: 6lb 3.8oz (trail), 7.67 lbs (packed)", "Doors: 2, plus 2 vestibules", full-coverage waterproof rainfly included, DAC Pressfit poles, and a "3-season" rating. CleverHiker's Sept 25, 2024 review corroborated the same 3-person model (dims "90 x 68 x 48 in.", peak 48 in, footprint included) and is the price source, stating "Price: $400". Mountain Hardwear's own product pages (standard 2102591 and all-season 2063621) both returned a 404 error page and REI 403'd, so a dated review was used as the primary source; the standard 3-season Mineral King 3 was verified as distinct from the separate "Mineral King 3 All Season" variant.

products.name: Sea to Summit Telos TR2 Tent
products.priceNote: MSRP $449 for the standard Telos TR2, stated verbatim on CleverHiker Quick Specs ("Price: $449") and Better Trail ("at $449, it doesn't offer a clear advantage"). The 2026 successor Telos TR2 Evo is $530 per Better Trail — that is a different model, not this one.
products.provenance: CleverHiker's dated review (last updated Oct 18, 2024) covers the exact standard Sea to Summit Telos TR2 and confirms verbatim: Price $449, Packed Weight 3 lb 11 oz (= 3.69 lb), Dimensions 84.5 x 53 x 43 in, freestanding, peak "43.5 inches tall," a full-mesh two-door body ("Either door on the rainfly"), 20D floor and 15D ripstop nylon fly. Better Trail's review corroborates the spec table verbatim — Packaged weight 3 lb 11 oz, Floor Area 28 sq. ft., Floor dimensions 84.5 x 53/43 in, Peak height 43.5 in, 20D nylon floor, full-coverage 3-season rainfly, $449 — and its editor's note explicitly distinguishes this original TR2 from the 2026 Telos TR2 Evo successor ($530, 3 lb 9.3 oz), confirming model identity. Sea to Summit's own site now lists only the Telos Evo (original TR2 product URLs redirect to the homepage/collection), so no live manufacturer page exists for this superseded model; both dated reviews were fetched verbatim via fetch-clean. releaseDate/release left null because neither fetched page states the original TR2's launch year.

products.name: Kelty Wireless 6 Tent
products.priceNote: Kelty.com MSRP $279.95 (listed on manufacturer product page as "Wireless 6P Tent $279.95"); CleverHiker's dated review lists $280.
products.provenance: Kelty.com product page ("Wireless 6P Tent") directly confirmed model identity and specs verbatim: MSRP $279.95, Capacity 6, No. of Doors 2, Packed Weight 19 lb, Floor Area 86.5 ft², Peak Height 74", 2 vestibules, fully taped seams and an included tent fly. CleverHiker's dated May 12, 2026 review corroborated the exact model — 86.5 sq ft floor, 74-in peak, $280 price, and described it as a "strictly a car camping" three-season family tent with a rainfly. Model confirmed as the current 6-person Wireless (floor 86.5 ft² / peak 74 in / 118x106x74 dims match on both pages), not the Wireless 8P ($389.95) or another capacity; seasons "3-season" and type "car_camping" taken from CleverHiker, releaseDate null (no explicit release year stated on either fetched page).

products.name: Big Agnes Tiger Wall UL2 Tent
products.priceNote: US MSRP $499.95, verbatim on bigagnes.com official product page (SKU TTWUL225, "$499.95"); also listed "From $499.95" on the Big Agnes ultralight-tents collection. CleverHiker rounds it to $500.
products.provenance: Big Agnes' official product page confirms the exact model: title "Tiger Wall UL2 Ultralight Tent", SKU TTWUL225, MSRP $499.95, described verbatim as a "three-season, semi-freestanding, side-entry ultralight tent" with HyperBead fabric, DAC Featherlite poles, a "Side entry, dual-door design" (a door + vestibule on both sides = 2 doors), and 9 included stakes. CleverHiker's April 30, 2025 hands-on review (corroboration) lists the same UL2 at $500 with Packed Weight 2 lb. 8 oz. (2.5 lb), dimensions 86 x 52/42 x 39 in (39 in peak height), and "28 square feet of floor space" — the numeric weight/floor/height that the manufacturer keeps behind a collapsed specs tab. Both sources are unambiguously the 2-person UL2 (not UL1/UL3, Platinum, or mtnGLO); price is taken verbatim from Big Agnes and weight/floor/height verbatim from CleverHiker. No explicit product release year is published on either fetched page, so release/releaseDate are left null.
